What is the following text, and where does it come from?

<text>
Summary of policy proposals (2001)

- Constitutional and governance
  - Seek a referendum on full self-government and expanded powers for the Scottish Parliament.
  - Create a written constitution; inclusive citizenship based on residence, birth, or parentage; retain the monarchy subject to referendum.
  - Introduce proportional representation at all levels; reform and reduce quangos; strengthen parliamentary oversight.
  - Ensure civil service career continuity and advancement in Scotland.

- Economy, investment, and taxation
  - Establish a sovereign wealth-style fund using surplus oil revenues (Scottish Fund for Future Generations).
  - Create a public, not-for-profit infrastructure financier (Scottish Trust for Public Investment) to replace high-cost PFI/PPP.
  - Conduct a comprehensive tax review focused on fairness, simplicity, and business competitiveness; no overall tax rise without mandate.
  - Immediate measures: cut fuel duty by 10p/gal, funded by a new 5p income tax band on earnings over £100,000; consider small business rates relief; review local government finance, including local income tax.

- Jobs, wages, and enterprise
  - Raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages, with support for small firms via tax measures; strengthen trade union rights through a statutory charter.
  - Devolve and refocus employment programs toward training and job black spots.
  - Invest in transport, digital connectivity, and skills; streamline development agencies; integrate tourism promotion into the enterprise network.

- Education and children
  - Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants; support Cubie recommendations on student benefits.
  - Create an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18 in stages; end league tables; cut assessment burdens; major school refurbishment via the public investment trust.
  - Lower voting age to 16; implement UNCRC; establish a Children’s Commissioner; expand Gaelic-medium education; support inclusive education and anti-racism.

- Health and social care
  - Form a National Health Care Commission to set strategy and end postcode treatment by making HTBS decisions binding; increase HTBS budget.
  - Public health: free fruit in primary schools; nutritional standards for school meals.
  - Reintroduce free dental check-ups; freeze and review prescription charges.
  - Invest via the public investment trust; audit and modernize equipment; £4m Clean Hospitals Fund; recruit at least 1,500 nurses; halve maximum inpatient waits; provide free personal care for older people.

- Environment, energy, and water
  - Climate risk assessment and a National Environment Plan; target 12% of total energy (25% of electricity) from renewables by 2010.
  - No new nuclear plants; decommission existing sites; develop decommissioning expertise.
  - Promote waste reduction and polluter-pays principles; review climate levy impacts on hydro.
  - Review water industry finances to curb charge increases; enhance democratic control; protect low-income users; seek Competition Act exemption.

- Justice, drugs, and policing
  - Fund 1,000 additional police officers; establish a Sentencing Advisory Panel; speed up lower courts.
  - Expand drug courts; strengthen rehabilitation and family support.
  - Parental compensation orders for youth damage (with safeguards).
  - Lifetime supervision for high-risk violent/sexual offenders; implement Maclean recommendations; strengthen sex offender registration.

- Social policy, equality, and immigration
  - National anti-poverty strategy with “poverty-proofing”; shift social inclusion admin funds to frontline services.
  - Fast and fair asylum decisions; oppose voucher-based support.
  - Strengthen disability rights (extend DDA scope; introduce a disability equality indicator).

- Housing and communities
  - Press for UK assumption of historic council housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via the public investment trust.
  - Oppose wholesale stock transfer; support tenant-focused, tenure-neutral policy; three-year core funding for voluntary sector; exempt charities from water charges.
  - Tackle rough sleeping and hidden homelessness.

- Rural, agriculture, fisheries, and land
  - Immediate 10p/gal fuel duty cut; improve rural transport and digital access; protect post offices, schools, and links.
  - Post–foot and mouth agricultural review; tighten import controls and origin labelling; support diversification and organics; renegotiate Less Favoured Areas terms.
  - Fisheries: compensated tie-ups; technical conservation; devolved leadership in EU talks; reform CFP toward zonal management; support processing and aquaculture.
  - Independent inquiry on salmon farming; strengthen environmental regulation; enhance SEPA resources.
  - Expand community land rights and participation; develop a national freshwater fisheries policy.

- Europe, defence, and international
  - Support EU membership with stronger subsidiarity; consider euro entry subject to conditions and referendum.
  - Remove nuclear weapons from Scotland; oppose US missile defence; create a professional Scottish Defence Force; phased withdrawal from NATO while maintaining cooperation.
  - Refocus external representation on trade, investment, and tourism; raise aid toward UN targets; cancel debt; untie aid; coordinate NGOs via “Aid from Scotland.”

- Transport and connectivity
  - Use the public investment trust for rail electrification (including East Coast), airport rail links, Borders rail, and key bottlenecks; create Regional Transport Authorities; single multimodal safety body; keep air traffic control public; public stake in Railtrack for accountability.
  - National concessionary travel for youth, students, older and disabled people; explore light rail.
  - Reduce ferry fares via Road Equivalent Tariff pilots; abolish Skye Bridge tolls; airports review to increase direct European flights and reduce fares.

- Culture, language, broadcasting, and sport
  - Devolve broadcasting oversight; accelerate digital rollout; increase autonomy for national public broadcaster.
  - Reform arts funding; establish a national theatre and a “Scottish Academy”; boost traditional arts; create a national lottery.
  - Support Gaelic and Scots languages in education and media.
  - Prioritize community sport; support football academies; bid to host major tournaments.

- Pensions and social security
  - Restore the earnings link for the basic state pension, using NI Fund surplus; protect those near tax thresholds; aim to align basic pension with MIG over time.
  - Streamline benefits delivery into a single agency; simplify housing benefit and use it to lower housing costs; improve disability benefit processing; consider extending winter fuel payments to severely disabled under 60; review support for 16–17 year olds; improve Working Families Tax Credit design and uptake.
</text>
